topics.description: Chilean military dictator who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990 after the coup that overthrew Salvador Allende and oversaw the repression of political dissidents.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A leader of this county committed suicide with an AK-47 in the La Moneda palace. In 1973, a CIA-backed coup overthrew that socialist leader, Salvador Allende, after he nationalized this country’s copper mines in the (*) Atacama Desert. Dissidents were brutally suppressed during the dictatorship of Austugo Pinochet in, for 10 points, what South American country led from Santiago?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this country, “el ladrillo” detailed the economic policies advocated by the Chicago Boys. This country’s  copper industry was nationalized by a socialist leader who committed suicide at La Moneda Palace, (*) Salvador Allende. A longtime dictator of this country may have ordered the assassination of Pablo Neruda. For 10  points, name this South American country formerly led by Augusto Pinochet, which is governed from Santiago.

topics.description: The New Kingdom Egyptian pharaoh who fought at Kadesh, made a peace treaty with the Hittites, and commissioned monuments including Abu Simbel.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler crossed the Orontes (ore-AHN-tayz) to defeat the Hittite ruler Hattusili (HAT-tus-EE-lee) III in the largest chariot battle in history. That Battle of Kadesh was followed by this ruler signing the first known peace treaty. This New Kingdom ruler built his wife Nefertari the largest tomb in the Valley of the Queens, as well as the temple complex of (*) Abu Simbel. For ten points, name this Egyptian pharaoh known as “the Great.”
parts.answer: Ramses the Great [or Ramses II or Ozymandias]

topics.description: The vast Eurasian empire founded by Genghis Khan in the 13th century and later divided into successor khanates, including the Yuan dynasty in China.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The paiza metal pendant was carried by messengers of these people’s Yam postal system. Leaders of these people were elected by a Kurultai. A non-Byzantine Secret History chronicles the rise of these people’s first leader, who was born with the name (*) Temujin. These people ruled China through the Yuan dynasty of Kublai. For 10 points, the empire of what East Asian people was founded by Genghis Khan?

parts.label: L
parts.question: This empire's first ruler was Genghis Khan. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this largest contiguous land empire in world history. It stretched from Siberia to Eastern Europe, eventually fracturing into several smaller realms such as the Chagatai Khanate.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This grandson of Genghis established the Yuan Dynasty in China, becoming the first non-Han emperor to control all of China after his conquest of the Song Dynasty and accession to the imperial throne.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This successor state of the Mongol Empire was founded by Batu Khan and ruled over the steppes of Eastern Europe and Central Asia. It was eventually defeated by Muscovy at the Great Stand on the Ugra River.
parts.answer: the Golden Horde [or Altan Ord, or Altın Urda, or Ulug Ulus, or the Ulus of Jochi, or the Kipchak Khanate; prompt on the Great Horde]

topics.description: Soviet statesman who served as the final leader of the Soviet Union and pursued glasnost and perestroika while helping ease the Cold War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: While running to become governor of this state, a future president promised to “clean up the mess” at its state university’s original and flagship campus, though his actions partly led to the People’s Park protests. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this US state currently led by Gavin Newsom, who lives just outside of its city of Sacramento.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This governor of California later became the 40th president of the United States. This president fired thousands of striking air traffic controllers and created a missile defense program nicknamed “Star Wars”.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Reagan discussed “Star Wars,” his Strategic Defense Initiative, at the Geneva Summit with this last Soviet General Secretary. This leader’s policies of glasnost and perestroika foreshadowed the end of the Soviet Union.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man spoke against “socialized medicine” in a campaign dubbed “Operation Coffee Cup.” Before a debate, this man promised not to “exploit” the “youth and inexperience” of his fifty-six-year-old opponent. This man described a group of people as having “Slipped the surly bonds of Earth to touch the face of God” in one speech and endorsed Barry Goldwater in his “A (*) Time For Choosing” speech. In a reelection ad, this man claimed it was “Morning in America,” and called upon one world leader to “Open this gate” in Berlin. For 10 points, name this President during the Challenger disaster, who asked Mikhail Gorbachev to “Tear down this wall!”

topics.description: A heavily armed infantryman of ancient Greece who fought with a spear, shield, armor, and commonly in a phalanx formation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This metal alloy was used by cultures like Hyksos, Assyrians, and the Middle Kingdom of Egypt. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this alloy, primarily made with copper and tin, that was used throughout the ancient world to make weapons and tools.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This weapon became an extremely popular bronze weapon for warriors. Bronze’s strength allowed for smiths to create this weapon with a longer blade than daggers or knives.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] These Greek soldiers used bronze shields, called hoplons, which are the origin of their name. These soldiers often entered battle in organized formations called phalanxes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this battle was won by an alliance of Athenian and Plataean [pla-TAY-un] warriors, news of the result was very quickly sent to Athens by a single runner, who legendarily dropped dead on arrival. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 490 BCE battle that inspires the name of a modern, 26-mile-long footrace.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This is the Greek term for a spear-and-shield wielding footsoldier. Ten thousand of these soldiers from Athens joined another thousand from Plataea at Marathon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hoplite soldiers became much more effective after they adopted this defensive formation, which was first used against a foreign enemy at Marathon. In this formation, hoplites are arrayed in long lines, with each using their shield to protect both themselves and the hoplite on their left.

topics.description: King of England from 1377 to 1399 who was deposed by Henry Bolingbroke after conflicts involving the Lords Appellant and his royal favorites.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Robert de Vere and other favorites of a king of this name were sentenced to death after the rebellion of the Lords Appellant. Another king of this name likely employed members of the Assassins to kill Conrad of Montferrat. A king of this name was deposed by Henry Bolingbroke, the son of John of Gaunt. A king of this name was captured and (*) ransomed for 150,000 marks by Leopold of Austria, whom he had earlier insulted at the siege of Acre. That king of this name captured Jaffa after defeating Saladin during the Third Crusade, which he led with Philip II and Frederick Barbarossa. For 10 points, give this regnal name of the English king nicknamed “Lion Heart.”
parts.answer: Richard [accept Richard I or Richard II or Richard Couer-de-Leon or Richard the Lion Heart]

topics.description: The last Yorkist king of England, whose defeat and death at the Battle of Bosworth Field ended the Wars of the Roses.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One leader in this conflict adopted the symbol of the sun in splendor after seeing an atmospheric phenomenon called a sun dog at the Battle of Mortimer’s Cross. According to a report by Prospero di Camulio, another leader in this conflict sang under a tree for the duration of this conflict’s Second Battle of St. Albans. (*) Anne Neville’s successive marriages to combatants on both sides of this conflict corresponded with her father Warwick’s shifting allegiances. This conflict ended with the battle of Bosworth Field, where Henry Tudor defeated Richard III. For 10 points, name this series of 15th century conflicts between York and Lancaster named for a type of flower.

topics.description: The Third Crusade was the 1189–1192 campaign by European rulers, including Richard the Lionheart and Frederick Barbarossa, against Saladin to recover Jerusalem.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler was imprisoned by Leopold of Austria on charges of murdering Conrad of Montferrat. This monarch conquered Cyprus from the Byzantines and sold it to the Templars. This monarch took over leadership of the Third (*) Crusade from Philip II and fought against Saladin. The son of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine was, for 10 points, what 12th-century English king named "the Lionheart"?
parts.answer: Richard I [accept Richard the Lionheart or Richard Cœur de Lion; prompt on Richard until "Lionheart" is read and accept afterwards]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This emperor convened the Diet of Roncaglia after crushing Milan. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Holy Roman Emperor who drowned in the Saleph River, nicknamed for his beard.
parts.answer: Frederick Barbarossa [accept Frederick I; prompt on Frederick]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Frederick Barbarossa’s death occurred as he was traveling to this conflict, in which Richard the Lionheart led forces against Saladin.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Frederick Barbarossa was excommunicated by the third pope of this name, often adopted by wannabe imitators of a “Great” Macedonian conqueror of this name.
parts.answer: Alexander [or Alexander III; or Alexander the Great]

topics.description: The 1917–1922 conflict in Russia between the Bolshevik Red Army and anti-Bolshevik forces, following the Russian Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these people, Li Zongren, allied the Guangxi [gwan-shee] Clique with the Chinese government during the Northern Expedition, but later fought them in the Central Plains War. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these local rulers who controlled China during a namesake “era” after the fall of the Qing Dynasty.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The warlord Zhang Zongchang [jung jong-chang] made use of armored trains manned by refugees from this conflict who settled in Harbin. The Bolsheviks murdered Tsar Nikolai II during this conflict.
parts.answer: Russian Civil War [prompt on the Russian Revolution]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Zhang fled into exile after his army was crushed by this political party’s National Revolutionary Army. Sun Yat-sen founded this party during the 1911 Revolution.
parts.answer: Kuomintang [or KMT or Guomindang or GMD; or the Chinese Nationalist Party]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Fridtjof Nansen (FRIT-juf NAAN-sin) won the 1922 Nobel Peace Prize for mitigating one of these  events in the Povolzhye (PAH-volzh-yeh) region. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this type of event that occurred between 1921 and 1922 in Russia. A later one of these events  was the main cause of death during the Holodomor (HAH-luh-doh-MOR) in Ukraine.
parts.answer: famines [prompt on descriptions such as lack of food or mass starvations; prompt on  droughts; prompt on failed harvests]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The famine of 1921 followed this conflict, which was fought between the White Army and the  Bolshevik Red Army.
parts.answer: Russian Civil War [or Grazhdanskaya voyna v Rossii]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Vladimir Lenin's New Economic Policy was decreed amid the famine and after this mutiny against  the Bolshevik government. Stepan Petrichenko (STEP-in pet-rish-ENK-oh) led this rebellion at a port city  on Kotlin Island.

topics.description: An intergovernmental organization established after World War I to promote collective security and international cooperation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s emperor, Menelik II, stopped an Italian invasion of his country at the Battle of Adwa. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Along with Liberia, what nation in the Horn of Africa led from Addis Ababa is considered to be the only African nation not to be colonized?

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Emperor Halie Selassie protested a later Italian attempt to colonize Ethiopia with an impassioned speech to this international organization, which Woodrow Wilson called for in his Fourteen Points.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In his speech to the League of Nations, Selassie decried the use of these kinds of weapons against his people. Examples of these weapons include nerve gas and mustard gas.
